narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Mostly dry conditions will persist across Kisumu through tonight. Thunder possible, peaking tomorrow evening. Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with rain possible from Monday and thunderstorms likely each day.

## Today's Forecast
Warm temperatures and partly cloudy skies characterize the evening across Kisumu, following an observed afternoon high of 31°C / 88°F and heading toward an overnight low of 19°C / 66°F. Conditions tonight remain mostly dry, though isolated light showers (around 0.3 mm / 0.01 in) cannot be completely ruled out. Peak background wind gusts on land will reach up to 40 km/h (22 kt). Overnight cloud cover will fluctuate between broken cloud and clearer intervals. Solar UV exposure has ended for the day following sunset. Air quality ground sensors report moderate conditions, with AQI readings spanning from 42 to 55; Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central recorded the highest reading at 55 AQI.

## Extended Outlook
On Sunday and Monday, conditions remain warm with daytime highs near 31°C / 88°F to 33°C / 91°F and overnight lows around 19°C / 66°F. Rain probability increases by Monday, with scattered showers and thunderstorms becoming possible. By Tuesday (Day+3), high temperatures show a wide model spread ranging from 28°C / 82°F to 34°C / 93°F under predominantly overcast skies, with widespread showers and thunderstorms likely (around 7.0 mm / 0.28 in total precipitation). From Wednesday through Saturday (Days 4 to 7), daytime highs stabilize around 29°C / 84°F to 31°C / 88°F. Convective instability remains elevated across the extended period, maintaining a daily potential for afternoon and evening thunderstorms.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Elevated convective instability is present overnight into Sunday, with atmospheric CAPE levels exhibiting significant model disagreement: GFS indicates modest instability around 430 J/kg, while ECMWF and ICON build to 1430–1460 J/kg, and UKMO peaks at 2780 J/kg. While widespread heavy rainfall is not expected tonight, any isolated shower or thunderstorm that develops can generate sudden, localized wind gusts far exceeding the background forecast speed. Anyone outdoors or on open ground should monitor local sky conditions.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Overnight conditions across Winam Gulf remain mostly calm with peak background gusts near 29 km/h (16 kt). However, high CAPE values over the basin support potential nocturnal convective activity. Boaters should exercise caution, as isolated thunderstorms can trigger abrupt, strong downdraft gusts and localized choppy water even when background winds are light.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1019 hPa) — a 9 hPa spread, representing a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is falling toward the east, north, northwest, south, and southeast, while overhead pressure in the Nyanza Basin is also falling (1014.8 hPa mean). Regional MSLP across the basin points will continue a gradual deepening trend over the next 24 to 72 hours down to 1011–1013 hPa, maintaining favorable synoptic support for moisture convergence and convective development.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecast weighting today favors ICON for precipitation calls, as the long-run review establishes ICON as the strongest rainfall caller at Day+0 (82% historical accuracy) compared to GFS (64%). UKMO and GFS systematically under-forecast surface wind gusts at Day+0, which supports utilizing the calibrated land peak gust figure of 40 km/h (22 kt). The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) local bulletin calls for a maximum temperature of 29°C / 84°F, a minimum of 20°C / 68°F, and sunny intervals with a chance of light afternoon showers; this is closely aligned with the multi-model numerical guidance.

earlier_issuances.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Largely dry, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. Temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with rain possible from Monday and thunderstorms likely each day.

## Today's Forecast
Temperatures reaching a daytime high of 29.5°C / 85°F expected today, with overnight lows falling to 18.5°C / 65°F. Sunny intervals through early afternoon give way to increasing cloud cover by late afternoon. Light rain or scattered showers are expected from the late afternoon into the evening, with isolated thunderstorms possible, peaking after dusk. Surface winds turn north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with calibrated peak gusts reaching 41 km/h (22 kt). Solar radiation peaks with a Very High UV index of 8.8 around midday. Air quality remains in the Moderate range (US AQI 42 to 100), with the highest concentration recorded at Kisumu Airport.

## Extended Outlook
On Sunday (2026-09-20), conditions remain mostly dry and warm with temperatures around 31°C / 88°F. Rain chances return on Monday (2026-09-21) and Tuesday (2026-09-22), with thunderstorms likely each day as instability increases across the basin. Models show a wide spread in Day+3 maximum temperatures, ranging from 30°C / 86°F to 34°C / 93°F. Looking further ahead into Wednesday through Friday, unsettled convective activity continues with periodic shower risk, before clearer skies return by Saturday.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability develops from late morning and peaks during the evening hours. UKMO and ECMWF show substantial energy with peak CAPE values reaching 2210 J/kg and 2010 J/kg respectively, whereas GFS indicates weaker instability near 400 J/kg. While overall precipitation totals remain modest (around 2.0 mm / 0.08 in), any localized convective cell can generate sudden, strong downdraft gusts well above the background wind forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Winds on Winam Gulf follow a marked lake-breeze pattern: overnight at 5 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt), then southwesterly into the evening at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt). Peak gusts across the open water are expected to reach 29 km/h (16 kt). Boaters should remain alert for sudden, violent wind shifts and isolated strong gusts accompanying evening thunderstorms.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1019 hPa) — a 9 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the east, north, northwest, south, southeast — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is falling. Across the local Nyanza Basin, mean pressure sits near 1014.7 hPa with a 24-hour falling trend of -1.2 hPa, favoring afternoon convective development.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
The numerical guidance behind this issuance is at least 15 hours old. Model weighting favors ECMWF and ICON for rainfall probability and instability timing, given ICON's established record as the top Day+0 rain caller and GFS's tendency to under-forecast peak wind. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) local bulletin forecasts a high of 29.0°C / 84°F and a low of 20.0°C / 68°F with sunny intervals and afternoon light showers over a few places, which aligns closely with the multi-model consensus. Ground air quality stations report US AQI values of 42 at Ochieng' Avenue, 58 at Dunga Beach, and 100 at Kisumu Airport.
